Telegram._UserTenantMappings_doc: Local dev sample mapping for /start onboarding. The single key '12345' is also listed under Telegram:AllowedUserIds above so a developer running `dotnet user-secrets set Telegram:BotToken ...` and pointing their Telegram account (after editing the user id to match theirs) to this worker via polling can drive a single-workspace /start end-to-end on their laptop. Multi-workspace bindings are demonstrated in appsettings.json -- copy that shape here if you need to exercise the workspace-disambiguation inline keyboard locally.

OutboundQueue._Mode_doc: Stage 6.3 IOutboundQueue selection switch -- 'InMemory' selects the bounded Channel<OutboundMessage>-backed dev queue per the brief's 'Create appsettings.Development.json with ... in-memory queue' requirement. Program.cs reads this value via the OutboundQueue:Mode key and calls services.UseInMemoryOutboundQueue() to Replace() the EF-backed PersistentOutboundQueue that AddMessagingPersistence installs by default.
